title: Model availability forecasting and procurement-trigger catalog
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: Create an operational catalog that (1) forecasts near-term availability risk for prioritized open and commercial model variants and (2) defines procurement / mitigation triggers and standardized response playbooks for enterprise customers.

Background: Sales & Customer Success have reported increasing friction when a widely used model variant is temporarily unavailable or when new license/hosting restrictions appear. Engineering needs clear procurement signals and procurement needs repeatable decision rules so we can move faster without ad-hoc escalations. This ticket operationalizes market signals (model releases, deprecation notices, license changes, regional supply outages) into forecasted availability risk and procurement triggers.

Scope:
- Target models: curated set (top 20 models by customer usage + 10 vendor-priority models)
- Time horizon: 0-3 months (tactical) and 3-12 months (planning)
- Outputs: forecast matrix (availability probability by week), procurement-trigger catalog (conditions -> action), response playbooks (procurement request template, temporary fallback configuration, customer communication template)

Deliverables:
1) A CSV/JSON feed spec for availability signals and model meta (model id, variant, hostability, license, region coverage, recent incident count)
2) A prioritized list of models with 0-90 day availability score and risk band (green/amber/red)
3) Procurement-trigger catalog: boolean and threshold-based triggers (e.g., "license_clause_change=true", "regional_capacity_drop>=30% for 48h", "incident_count_7d>=3") mapped to actions (procurement RFP, contract extension, pin-to-legacy, customer notification)
4) Three operational runbooks (short emergency, mid-term procurement, and communications) with owners & SLAs
5) Dashboard wireframe in Console showing live risk heatmap, active triggers, and recent mitigation actions

Methodology:
- Signals: model release RSS, vendor status pages, cloud region capacity metrics, internal telemetry (customer callouts, usage spikes), public issue trackers, procurement/legal flags
- Heuristics + simple scoring: combine signal weights into an availability probability; validate with historical incidents (backtest using past 6 months of telemetry)
- Threshold tuning: iterate with Sales/Success on false positive / false negative tolerance

Acceptance criteria:
- Feed spec documented and implemented as a JSON example in Drive (link below)
- Backtest demonstrates >60% precision at predicting customer-impacting unavailability in 0-14 day horizon on historical data
- Runbooks reviewed and signed off by Eng lead and Legal (procurement templates present)
- Dashboard wireframe reviewed by Console PM and assigned to a Console design ticket

Links & artifacts:
- Spec draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1z_example_model-availability-spec
- Historical incident dataset (internal): https://bigquery.redwood.ai/datasets/model_incidents_2025
- Example procurement PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427

Risks & open questions:
- Data quality: some vendor status pages are intermittent; need fallback heuristics
- Legal sensitivity: automated procurement triggers need human approval gates for high-dollar contracts
- SLO alignment: which internal SLAs should this system prioritize (Dedicated vs Hosted customers)?

Next steps:
- Run a 1-week spike to assemble signals and run backtest (owner: Eng telemetry)
